files.README.md:
# Cransley Bottling - label applicator

The bottling hall's label applicator writes a line to logs/labeller.log for every
event it handles:

    <UTC time> <event> ...

LOAD records a new label reel being spliced in and names the reel. JAM is
written each time the web jams and records the fault code and the print offset
the web had reached. A run of jams started on 17 September 2026 and the shift
report has to trace them to the label stock that was in the applicator, whose
core diameter the applicator's spindle has to match; the goods-in book in
notes/reel-intake.md lists each reel received with its core and width.
files.notes/reel-intake.md:
# label stock received

Every consignment of label reels booked in at goods-in. `core` is the internal
diameter of the reel's core, which the applicator's spindle has to match.

| reel    | core (mm) | width (mm) | received   |
| ------- | --------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| RL-8120 | 76        | 320        | 2026-09-11 |
| RL-8144 | 40        | 260        | 2026-09-15 |
| RL-8219 | 76        | 300        | 2026-09-16 |
| RL-8177 | 152       | 420        | 2026-09-17 |
| RL-8203 | 76        | 380        | 2026-09-21 |

turns.prompt: Cransley Bottling's label applicator writes a line whenever it splices in a new reel or the label web jams, and a run of jams began on 17 September 2026 that the shift report has to trace back to the label stock. What was the core diameter, in millimetres, of the reel that was in the applicator when the jams began? Give the number alone, as digits, with no label. Reply with only the final answer. If you cannot determine the answer, reply exactly UNKNOWN.
